parts.text: Globally, a quarter of wild-caught fish are processed into fishmeal and fish oil, and only a small share

from West Africa. Most is used in animal feed, with aquaculture accounting for the largest share. These provide valuable nutrients, particularly in early-life-stage diets and for carnivorous species such as salmon and shrimp, while contributing to the

low carbon footprint of farmed seafood.

The supply of marine ingredients is highly regulated and fairly stable but should not be taken for granted. Climate change and warming periods such as El Niño can weaken the

of nutrient-rich waters from the deep sea. This reduces the availability of plankton and fish and limits the supply of marine ingredients required for aquaculture.

This means we need to make the best use of the resources already available. Fish processing

(including heads, guts and skeletons) are playing an increasingly important role, accounting for 34% of global fishmeal production and 54% of fish oil supply in 2024.

A new era of supply chain risk

Marine ingredients from potentially

sources have slipped through the net despite responsible sourcing claims. One 2025 investigation found that certified Turkish-farmed seabass sold by major retailers in Europe was fed fishmeal sourced from three factories in Senegal that have been

to food insecurity and job losses in local communities.

One way to reduce risk in aquaculture feed supply chains is to source ingredients domestically. But this is easier said than done. Aquafeed supply chains are

on the global trade in marine and terrestrial ingredients and thus face challenges related to scale, cost, nutritional quality and environmental sustainability.

While marine ingredients can be sustainably sourced and continue to be

to the global food system, it’s important to use them in efficient ways that maximise their contribution to human nutrition. Certification programmes currently focus on ensuring that fish are caught or farmed responsibly. The environmental and social safeguards include stock

, environmental footprint and making sure workers are treated fairly.

The certification programmes pay less attention to food security and critics argue they favour export markets and

over local communities. As a result, calls are growing for broader measures of what constitutes truly sustainable and ethical seafood.

Use nutrients wisely

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Climate-related risks discourage investment in poorer countries and can also harm corporations.
Aquaculture can contribute to food security while reducing pressure on valuable wild fish resources.
Consumers' ideas about organic food do not always match what labels and standards communicate.
Victorian spiritualism turned the desire to communicate beyond death into commercial opportunities.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Most species used in the marine ingredients industry have low market appeal and limited consumer demand, meaning that diverting fish from feed to food does not automatically improve food security.

questions.prompt: What trend in wild fish catches for marine ingredients is reported?
options: The complete end of all fishing before aquaculture began
An unlimited and uninterrupted increase everywhere
No relationship to any discussion of fish resources
An overall decline despite the growth of aquaculture
questions.explanation: 第 3 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Despite its growth in the last three decades, global wild fish catches for marine ingredients have declined overall.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 8?
options: Traceability systems can play an important role, but they must do more than track supply chains.
Some scientists argue that fish, such as anchovies and mackerel, provide more essential nutrients when eaten directly rather than used as feed.
Globally, a quarter of wild-caught fish are processed into fishmeal and fish oil, and only a small share originates from West Africa.
Marine ingredients from potentially unsustainable sources have slipped through the net despite responsible sourcing claims.

questions.evidence: Marine ingredients from potentially unsustainable sources have slipped through the net despite responsible sourcing claims.
